summary: Register-only cold review (version 14, editorial.md 'Say what the texts say, plainly') of the expansive study src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/f01-christ-the-king (main.tex and sections 00, 05 editorial prose, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 80 notes, 90 apparatus), read completely with cat -n. Source verification, citations, chronology data, pagination and manifests were out of scope and not checked. The study still carries the register defects that the 21 October 2026 remediation named, several verbatim as the guidance's own examples ('Then the words on which the feast turns', 'The inheritance is not territory. It is ...', 'The Lamb receives an inheritance by dying, and the inheritance is mankind', 'The Preface gives the reading its order', 'The Offertory is the reading's centre'). All three interpretations end in the forbidden closing roll call ('every element of the formulary takes a place in one movement'); texts are credited with the study's inferences; antitheses are drawn against positions nobody holds, with a 'territory' refrain across three sections; paragraphs land on maxims or restate the quotation; 'reading(s)' for interpretations collides with the Mass's readings throughout, alongside 'formulary', 'element', 'witnesses', 'grammar', 'movement'; the date-and-location notes speak in pipeline terms (rows, records, bindings, elements); the comparison certifies Fathers' contributions and re-argues the first interpretation. The appointed-texts notes (05) are mostly plain apart from 'formulary' and 'element'. The apparatus (90) uses precise terms legitimately and shows no register leaking into it; its source-role disclosure has leaked into the body instead (10:161-162). Seven blocking findings, one advisory; all are sentence repairs with repair_target study.

findings.problem: All three interpretations still end in the closing roll call that the profile names as the defect (propers-three-documents.md, 'The expansive study'), and texts are credited with the study's own inferences or with links no source draws. Roll-call and lead instances: 20:202 heading 'How the whole Mass receives the kingdom'; 20:205-206 'every element of the formulary takes a place in one movement'; 20:8-10 'lets the whole formulary take its order from the Preface'; 20:209 'The Introit is the reading's text'; 20:239 'The Offertory is the reading's centre'; 20:248-249 'The Preface gives the reading its order' (the guidance's own example); 20:224 the Collect's petition is 'the inheritance asked for in the psalm, still being given'; 20:225 'The Epistle supplies the means and the moment of the receiving'; 20:243 'The Secret then names the asking that the Fathers found in verse 8'; 30:223 heading 'How the whole Mass claims the nations'; 30:226 'The Gospel is the reading's text'; 30:228-229 'The Gradual sets out the extent of the kingdom that the Gospel declares to be from above'; 30:240-242 Bellarmine's sense 'names the standard by which the kings of the Gradual are measured'; 30:258-260 the Secret: 'the nations' gathering is a gift given at the altar, not a conquest'; 30:260-262 'the first of them, regnum veritatis, is the truth to which the Gospel's King bears witness'; 30:214 'the formulary uses both'; 40:175 heading 'How the whole Mass moves toward the Father'; 40:9-11 'lets the Alleluia and the Communion say what kind of end that is'; 40:178 'The Preface is the reading's text'; 40:191 'The Epistle gives the head who goes first and brings the body after'; 40:199-200 the Collect asks for 'the work whose completion is the kingdom handed over'; 40:207-209 the Gradual's homage 'is the universal subjection that the Apostle's ... completes'; 40:210-211 the Gospel 'names a kingdom whose origin is the Father's, and its end is the Father's too'; 40:215 'The Secret shows the Priest still offering'; 50:5-6 'each lets a different element lead'. Credited links outside the roll calls: 10:259-260 the Secret asks 'the gifts that are the opposite of the Collect's wound'; 20:196 'The instituting act of the feast holds both titles together'; 30:204 'Quas primas holds the two halves in the same way'; 30:269-273 'Chrysostom's reasoning on Jn 18:36 shows what the figure cannot mean ... Hilary's reading of the second psalm shows what it can mean' (neither Father speaks of the Postcommunion); 40:127-128 the psalm 'carries in its full verse the flood'; 40:157 Bellarmine's phrase 'matches in thought' the Preface.
findings.required_result: Remove the three closing roll calls as roll calls. Keep each text's contribution only where the argument already uses it, give a lightly touched text a clause, and state every link between texts either as the named Father's or once as this interpretation's inference. No text is 'the reading's text/centre/order', and no text supplies, shows, names or completes what the study infers. Rewrites: 20:248-249 'The Preface gives the reading its order. The Son is anointed ...' -> 'The Preface puts the events in this order: the Son is anointed Priest and King, offers himself on the cross, and only then, all creatures subjected to him, hands over the kingdom.' 20:243 'The Secret then names the asking that the Fathers found in verse 8.' -> 'Taken this way, the Secret's offering of the hostia humanae reconciliationis is the asking Augustine finds in verse 8, the Son who offered himself in the stead of all sacrifices.' 30:258-260 -> 'The Secret asks for all nations the gifts of unity and peace.' (stop there). 40:210-211 -> 'In the Gospel the King says his kingdom is not hinc, and that he came to bear witness to the truth; Augustine and Hilary make the vision of that truth the handing over.' 30:269-273 -> 'The Postcommunion's soldiers are this interpretation's question, not Chrysostom's or Hilary's: taken with Chrysostom's point that Christ's kingship needs no servants who fight, and Hilary's kingdom where sin is overcome (Tract. in Ps. 2.42), the fighting is against sin.'

findings.problem: Antitheses against positions no source, text or reader puts forward, several carried from section to section as a refrain. 20:16 'The angels of the Introit are not praising God in the abstract.'; 20:32 'The question was not idle in the Church's history.'; 20:68-69 'And the inheritance is not territory. It is the nations baptized and taught' (verbatim the guidance's own example; Hilary's contrast is with the unjust right of earthly lords, not with territory); 40:180 'goods that belong to persons, not territory'; 50:54-55 'none of them lets it become a territory' (the 'territory' refrain runs through three sections); 30:242-243 'the throne of the Introit's antiphon belongs to the slain Lamb, not to a conqueror'; 30:244 'names the nations' condition as a wound, not a border'; 30:259-260 'a gift given at the altar, not a conquest'; 30:270-271 'the faithful's warfare is not his defence'; 30:291-293 'That service seeks no rival throne; it is a warfare against sin rather than with swords'; 50:34-35 'to fight sin, not with swords'. (The Gospel's own 'not of this world ... not from hence', Augustine's 'of/in' and 'from hence/here', Chrysostom's, Hilary's 'not his power, but us' and Cyril's 'not a servant ... but a Son' are the sources' antitheses and are not raised.)
findings.required_result: State Y without the X nobody holds; cut sentences that only deny. Rewrites: 20:68-69 -> 'The inheritance is the nations baptized and taught, carried over ex iniusto ... iure dominantium ...' (guidance's form). 30:244-247 -> 'The Collect says the nations are scattered by the wound of sin, peccati vulnere disgregatae, "a disruptive force" in Schuster's note, and asks that they be subjected to a most gentle rule, suavissimo imperio.' 20:16 -> begin 'The angels of the Introit stand round the throne at the moment the Lamb has taken the sealed book ...'. 30:291-293 -> 'It is fought against sin, under the standard of the Cross.' 50:54-55 -> 'All three identify the kingdom with the redeemed people, the Church.'

findings.problem: Paragraphs and sections land on a maxim, chiasmus or restatement of what the quotation has just said; deleting the last sentence loses nothing. 20:162-163 'The Lamb receives an inheritance by dying, and the inheritance is mankind.' (verbatim the guidance's example of a sentence one too late, after Victorinus); 20:37-39 'Read without that key, texts of receiving make the Son a creature promoted for his merits. Read with it, they speak of ...'; 20:107-110 'The double right removes the scandal of the Offertory. The Son does not ask because he lacks; he asks because ...'; 20:215-216 'He does not become what he was not; as man he is given to be what he had been before.' (third statement of Hilary's ut esset quod fuerat ante, after 20:63-65 and 20:193-194); 20:273 'Kingship is received through obedience unto death'; 30:70-71 'The kingdom gathers its people by truth heard and by grace, not by the strength of servants.'; 30:100-103 'A kingdom that takes its origin from one place in the world is bounded by that place. A kingdom that takes its origin from above is bounded by no place ...' (paraphrase of Aquinas's ubique just quoted); 30:143-145 'The distinction Augustine draws there ... is that the king serves God as a man by living faithfully, and as a king in the exercise of his office' (restates the quotation of 30:139 and is then restated by Aquinas's quotation); 30:208-210 'For the witnesses and the encyclical alike, the kingdom of the Gospel seeks no earthly throne, and the service of kings is owed to it' (thesis of 30:9-10 restated, again at 30:203-204 and 30:291); 30:220-221 'born of the Virgin to bear witness, or born King from eternity, he is the King whose kingdom is not from hence'; 30:247 'a rule whose instrument is its sweetness'; 30:297-298 'The mixed kingdom of this world becomes the manifest one, and the peace given in him becomes peace without storm.'; 40:4 'The end of Christ's kingship is the Father.' (pun on end, reprised at 40:210-211); 40:84-87 'his reign in them does not stop when they are delivered up, because he delivers them up by bringing them where he is'; 50:102-105 'Read together, the three readings say what the feast's Preface says in one sentence: ...' (the whole in miniature, and a re-argument of the thesis in the closer).
findings.required_result: End each paragraph when its information ends; cut the closer rather than polish it, and say each thesis once. Rewrites: 20:159-163 -> end at '... it was just that he be appointed heir and possess the human members (on Apoc 5:2-5).' 30:96-103 -> end at '... and the first half of Daniel's (Super Io. 18 lect. 6).' with the two 'A kingdom that takes its origin' sentences cut. 30:143-145 -> cut the paraphrase and go from the quotation to 'St Thomas reports the same distinction on Ps 2:10-11, ...'. 20:215-216 -> cut 'He does not become what he was not; ...'. 50:102-105 -> cut, or replace with a comparison not already made in the table and paragraphs above.

findings.problem: The production's working vocabulary runs through the reader prose. (a) 'reading(s)' for the study's interpretations, which collides with the Mass's own readings, especially in the element-by-element section where the Epistle and Gospel are being discussed: main.tex:16 subtitle 'a study of the proper in three readings'; 00:73 'each governs one of the readings that follow'; 00:95 'The three readings are complementary'; 10:7, 10:39 'the first reading below', 10:88 'the question of the second reading' (directly after the Collect, before the Epistle, the Mass's first reading), 10:156, 10:163, 10:217, 10:226-227 'is the text of the second reading', 10:296 'is the text of the third reading', 10:330, 10:346; 20:8, 213, 209, 239, 249; 30:212 'runs inside the reading', 30:218 'This reading rests', 30:226; 40:9, 119 'This reading puts', 178, 214; 50:1 running head 'Three Readings Compared', 50:5, 56, 58, 63, 72, 79, 86, 88, 90, 92, 95, 97, 102. (b) 'formulary': 00:68; 05:8, 05:17, 05:174 'The formulary has no Sequence', 05:328, 05:345; 10:99; 20:9, 20:205; 30:37 'the formulary's subjection', 30:195, 30:214; main.tex:8. (c) 'element': 05:7 'Every word of every element', 05:20 'the scriptural elements'; 10:2 heading 'Each Element in Its Setting'; 10:162; 20:205; 50:6. (d) 'witness(es)' as a term of art: 10:7, 10:46, 10:219 'divides the witnesses', 10:312, 10:330; 20:189; 30:39 'The witnesses of this Mass's texts refuse both', 30:209, 30:216; 40:128, 40:167 'The witnesses therefore give the Communion two moments', 40:227; 50:28 and 50:44 table rows 'Principal witnesses', 'Differences among its witnesses', 50:89. (e) metaphor terms: 00:73 'governs'; 20:206 'movement'; 20:141 'in the same grammar'; 20:41 'their answers carry over'; 40:128 'carries'; 10:161 'the one join', 10:288 'the same joining'. (Literal uses stand: 05:57 and 05:303 'The antiphon joins two verses', 40:92 Hilary's argument from the grammar of the verse, Bellarmine's own 'second reading' at 10:327.)
findings.required_result: Use the reader's words: 'interpretation' (or the interpretation's title) for the study's three lines of argument, 'the Mass', 'the texts', the element's own name ('the Collect'), and the Father's name for 'the witnesses'. Keep Introit, Secret, pericope etc., and leave precise terms to the apparatus. Rewrites: 00:73 'Three questions rise from these texts, and each governs one of the readings that follow.' -> 'These texts raise three questions, and each of the three interpretations that follow takes up one.' 10:88 'How a kingdom not of this world can ask the subjection of nations is the question of the second reading.' -> 'How a kingdom not of this world can ask the subjection of nations is taken up in the second interpretation (The Kingdom Not from Hence).' 10:219 "'For this was I born' divides the witnesses." -> "The Fathers divide over 'For this was I born'." 05:174 'The formulary has no Sequence.' -> 'The Mass has no Sequence.' 20:141 'St Bede reads the Apocalypse itself in the same grammar.' -> 'St Bede reads the Apocalypse in the same way, of what the Son receives in his humanity.' 10:2 -> 'Each Text in Its Setting'. main.tex:16 -> 'a study of the proper in three interpretations'.

findings.problem: The explanatory prose of the date-and-location appendix speaks in the production's data vocabulary rather than telling the reader what is dated and by whom: 80:6-7 'the date the Scripture chronology corpus gives for it'; 80:7-8 'Rows that share one answer name every element that uses it. The chronology record also carries the Tract'; 80:10 'The three orations and the Preface carry no biblical date'; 80:37-38 'share two rows. The "Historical setting" row records that no occasion is dated'; 80:43-44 'These attributions belong to the texts, and the dated reign of no king is attached to any of the three psalms here'; 80:53-54 'because the chronology record carries the Tract'; 80:58 'the setting the record gives'; 80:65 'They date a setting of a chant that this feast does not sing'; 80:71 'the chronology record holds no row for that year'; 80:83-85 'The traditional answer the row displays excludes the Antiochene date, and the critical answer the record holds offers no dated alternative for the book'; 80:89-91 'the chronology record has no element for it. The Apocalypse composition dates that the Introit's verses receive below are not extended by the record to Apoc 19:16'; 80:96-98 'binds that date to the passion narrative ... no event or binding reaches the questioning before Pilate ... and none is supplied here'. Records, rows, bindings, elements and what a record 'carries' or 'extends' are the pipeline's terms; the appendix belongs to the reader, and the 'Chronology' paragraph of the apparatus (90:65-71) is where the corpus mechanics belong.
findings.required_result: Rewrite the notes so their subjects are texts, events, dates and the authors who give them; refer to a table column by its printed heading only where the reader needs it, and move corpus mechanics to the apparatus. Rewrites: 80:71-73 -> 'Daniel dates the vision to the first year of Baltasar (7:1), a year given no date here; the setting dated is the seventy years of servitude to Babylon that Jeremias foretold (Jer 25:11-12), a duration rather than a year.' 80:96-98 -> 'The questioning before Pilate is not dated. John places it in the governor's hall at Jerusalem, early on the morning before the Pasch (18:28).' 80:83-85 -> 'The table gives Gigot's traditional date, and no date for the book on the later view.' 80:89-91 -> 'It is never said on this feast, and no date is given for Apoc 19:16.'

findings.problem: Coverage certification and the study's own reasoning narrated in the reader's hearing, and objections staged rather than taught. 50:62-70 'St Augustine contributes to all three readings: ... St Hilary also contributes to all three: ... St Thomas and St Robert Bellarmine contribute to all three' is a roll call certifying the review contract's two-Fathers requirement, not a comparison; 50:72-77 'The answers differ, and each would mislead on its own ... taken alone, would mislead ... taken alone, could leave ... taken alone, could pass over' stages failures of the study's own interpretations; 50:79-100 re-argues the first interpretation's objection and resolution from 20:165-194 ('The first reading grants that premise and refers the receiving to the humanity. Taken with Chrysostom, then, the verse states the first reading's premise and its objection at once') where a closing comparison should compare; 10:161-162 'That is the one join between two elements of the Mass that he makes himself' brings the apparatus's source-role disclosure (90:50-53) into the body; 30:33-39 'The question has two wrong answers, and the instituting act of the feast shows why both tempt ... Read alone ... read alone ... The witnesses of this Mass's texts refuse both'; 30:108-111 'That answer explains how the kingdom can be everywhere. It does not yet say what ... Here the same Fathers speak more concretely than a reader of the Gospel alone would expect'; 30:188 'The strongest difficulty is now plain.'
findings.required_result: State findings, not the method or the contract they satisfy. Cut the contribution roll call at 50:62-70 (the table already names principal Fathers); let the comparison say what the interpretations share and where they differ, once, without re-running 20:165-194. Rewrites: 10:157-163 -> 'He also treats the Gradual and the Alleluia together as "the double chant after the Epistle," a threefold catholicity: of place, ...; of subjects, ...; and of ages, ... (p. 203).' (end there). 30:108-111 -> 'Augustine, Aquinas and Bellarmine say what the kings and nations of the Gradual and the Offertory are to do.' 30:33-39 -> 'Quas primas calls it a grave error to say that Christ has no authority whatever in civil affairs, and draws from the feast a public duty of rulers towards him (nn. 17-19, 32); the Gospel's King also says his servants do not fight for him.' 50:72-77 -> cut, or state the substantive difference directly ('The first interpretation places the kingship received at the passion; the third, at the handing over; the second, in the present Church').

findings.problem: Asserted significance and performed emphasis recur from the opening onward. 00:33-34 'Then the words on which the feast turns:' (verbatim the guidance's own example); 10:37-38 'The verb that the antiphon sets at its centre'; 10:226 'the denial at its centre'; 30:96-97 'Then he draws the conclusion that resolves the apparent contradiction of the Mass'. Questions answered in the next breath rather than raised by the text: 20:59 'What was asked, and what was given? Hilary answers with ...'; 30:56 "What is the kingdom? 'Those who believe in Him,'". (The questions the texts themselves raise at 20:26-28 and 40:29-31, and Chrysostom's own question at 30:77, are not raised.)
findings.required_result: Say what the text does and who reads it so; let the argument bear the weight. Rewrites: 00:33-34 'Then the words on which the feast turns: "My kingdom ...' -> 'Jesus answers: "My kingdom ...' (guidance's form). 30:96-97 'Then he draws the conclusion that resolves the apparent contradiction of the Mass:' -> 'Then he concludes:'. 10:37-39 -> 'The antiphon's verb, accipere, and its object, divinitatem, are taken up in the first interpretation.' 30:56 -> 'The kingdom, Augustine says, is "those who believe in Him," ...'.

findings.problem: Isolated sentences that tell the reader nothing or disclaim a link instead of stating it. 10:284 'Schuster's commentary treats the Preface as a text.' adds nothing (the next sentence gives what Schuster says); 40:156-159 "His sweeping away of 'all power in general' matches in thought the Preface's ... and the Apostle's ... though Bellarmine does not cite that verse here" asserts a correspondence and disclaims it in one breath.
findings.required_result: Cut 10:284 and begin 'Schuster writes that the Preface's conception of Christ as Pontiff and King ...'. At 40:156-159 either state the inference once as this interpretation's ('Taken this way, Bellarmine's sweeping away of "all power in general" is the subjection of all creatures of which the Preface speaks') or cut the sentence.
